title: Chicken Alfredo Bake
subtitle: Creamy tray bake for seconds
description: Creamy tray bake for seconds. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Season and sear chicken
steps.instruction: Pat chicken dry; season with salt and pepper. Sear in olive oil until golden and 160°F; rest and slice or cube.

steps.title: Par-cook pasta
steps.instruction: Boil penne in well-salted water 2 minutes shy of al dente — it finishes in the oven. Drain thoroughly and spread on sheet pans so it does not clump before saucing.

steps.title: Make alfredo sauce
steps.instruction: Melt butter; cook garlic 30 seconds. Add cream and simmer; whisk in parmesan until silky. No crushed tomatoes — this is alfredo.

steps.title: Combine and pan up
steps.instruction: Toss pasta and chicken with alfredo. Transfer to buttered hotel pans; top with mozzarella.

steps.title: Bake until bubbling
steps.instruction: Bake at 375°F 20–25 minutes until cheese browns at edges.

steps.title: Serve Chicken Alfredo Bake
steps.instruction: Rest 5 minutes; scoop portions with a spatula. Finish with parsley.

proTips: Firefighters eat heavy after rough nights — double the protein if the hall had a busy shift.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Pull chicken at 160°F and let carryover hit 165°F — dry breast ruins crew morale.
tonightSpread: Plate Chicken Alfredo Bake with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Serve family-style from two full-size trays — never let the line run dry on a busy night.
Put starch and protein on separate trays so vegetarians can load up on sides.
Line up Chicken Alfredo Bake on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
Add a splash of stock or water when reheating — thick sauces tighten in the fridge.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Creamy tray bake for seconds. A hall pick for big-appetite nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
substitutions: Chicken thighs ↔ breasts (thighs forgive overcooking on the flat-top).
Any short pasta shape works — penne, rigatoni, or spaghetti.
